name: Spet Xyon Archers

abilities.name: Sea Sickness
abilities.text: As these men are inexperienced sailors. Caught up in sea combat, they suffer various penalties.

abilities.name: Precision Shot
abilities.text: Improved missile weapon damage for an extended period. These values are further modified by the unit itself.

abilities.name: Rapid Advance
abilities.text: Improved unit movement speed over an extended period.

attributes.name: Resistant to Fatigue
attributes.text: Fatigue has less of an effect on this unit.

attributes.name: Hide (forest)
attributes.text: This unit can hide in forests until enemy units get too close.

attributes.name: Fire Whilst Moving
attributes.text: This unit can fire when mounted and moving.

attributes.name: Parthian Shot
attributes.text: This unit can fire all around and not just in-front of itself.

short: Whether firing from a distance or charging in for the kill, foes rarely get a chance to lay eyes on these men.
history: The White Huns, like their more famous namesakes, were masters of mounted archery tactics. Their contact with so many different empires across the world made them familiar with the best aspects of many different military traditions, and enabled them to use the best of those to their advantage. Tactics from the Sassanid Persians (such as the Parthian shot), the Gupta Empire (inventors of the steel bow) and the wild, lawless steppes combined to create some of the most devastating missile troops imaginable. The skill required to fire a bow from a moving horse is phenomenal. Ancient cavalry archers had to keep control of their mounts with their knees whilst using both arms to fire their bows, which took a great deal of practice and physical strength. Often lightly armoured, horse archers were the ideal skirmish troops as they could quickly reach key areas of the battlefield to harass the enemy, but without getting so close they were forced into melee.
strengths: Very low damage and armour penetration
